D&D 5th Edition Westmarch Server (2014/5e)
docs.text:
Join The Starry Shore 2014/5e

Welcome to The Starry Shore Discover an endless number of worlds to explore at The Starry Shore! A place of respite adrift in the Astral Sea, the Starry Shore's magical barriers keep the typical dangers at bay, providing a sanctuary for any and all travelers who seek it. Adventure through new and exciting worlds via mysterious portals, or kick back with some friends and enjoy the Shore's amenities. We welcome travelers of all shapes and sizes and from all walks of life, so come let your imagination soar at The Starry Shore!

docs.title: How Things Work here?
docs.text:
Player Characters (PCs) live in The Starry Shore, an interplanar hub with the main street leading to many portals. Dungeon Masters create those portals leading to whatever worlds they dream up. PCs can visit those worlds via live sessions and/or text role play (TRP). PCs earn levels and gold via hours played in live or text sessions, and can level up beyond 20 by multiclassing, with no cap. Magic items are plentiful and most are easy to get.

and if you'd like to see how active the server is check out the 💬 session-log channel or the statistics in the 💬 announcements channel.

docs.title: What kind of D&D we play here?
docs.text:
Most of the games offered here are exciting one-shots, perfect for those who love spontaneous adventures. There are a few DMs that host campaigns, Typically, they like to play a few sessions with new players to see if there’s a good fit. If they like your gaming style, they might invite you to join a campaign. This server mainly focuses on these one-shot games, which make up the majority of our activities, allowing you to play on your own schedule.

We’re proud to say that our community only includes the coolest players. That said, we embrace diversity in play styles. Whether you’re someone who revels in rich storytelling and immersive roleplay, or a strategist who enjoys optimizing characters to their fullest potential, you’ll find a welcoming space here. Everyone is invited to bring their unique approach to the game.

docs.title: Modes of Play:
docs.text:
1. Live Voice Sessions: You gain "hours played", gold, and items as rewards from playing. (We use "hours played" in place of experience for leveling up.) This is the main method of play. And these kind of sessions can be anything, from lighthearted and funny to dark and serious.

  2. Text Roleplay: or TRP, there's 3 types of it:

  3. Live Trp sessions: same as live sessions, you play for a certain amount of hours but only trp, no vc needed!! rewards are the same hours and gold wise
  4. PBP/TRP in DMs worlds: This for casual trp, you can role play whenever you're free and the dm does the same, and you get some rewards out of it
  5. Trp for fun: This is the trp that happens inside the starry shore (crossroad category, VIP buildings) and it's just for fun, no rewards out of it
Sounds great! How do I start? You must be 18 years of age or older to play on the server. Then follow the steps in 💬 #getting-started channel to make a character.

docs.title: Member Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Have common sense, and follow the Server Code of Conduct.
  • You must be 18 years of age or older to play on the server (This is both for social and legal reasons. Sorry, no exceptions.).
  • PVP requires consent from both parties including the DM. Consent needs to be communicated, not just implied.
  • Sexual themes are not allowed until consent from the whole party is given.
  • Adult themes and language may appear. Our DM worlds' range from lighthearted and funny to dark and serious.
  • You need an approved character in order to play (see 💬 getting-started channel).
  • Players must track their characters (level, gold, items, etc) and keep this information updated in the player folder provided, as well as the relevant log channels.
  • In a rules dispute between a DM and Player, the DM’s word goes until the session is over and the staff can mediate.

[!question] Unsure of something? Ask away! Our community is welcoming, knowledgeable, and happy to help.

docs.title: Open Door Policy
docs.text: The staff team’s goal is to promote a safe and fun environment for all server members. You are invited to contact any staff through voice or private messages with questions or concerns as you see fit. You can submit your thoughts any time through the 💬 create-a-ticket ⁠channel, where the staff team will have access to it for review and response.

docs.title: Character Creation Steps
docs.text:
1. Make sure to watch our intro ▶ The Starry Shore Intro
🎥 Click here to watch the video

Then fill in this form to make a folder for you, which will appear in the Google Drive of the email that you provide. You only need to fill out this form once. A Google account is required to share your player folder with you. 📝 Fill Out the Google Form

📝 Click here to open the form without leaving this page Loading…
  1. (Make sure that you did step one :D) Create a level 3 character. Use 35 point buy, not stat rolls and fixed HP (do not roll for hit points). Use this calculator for your core stats: 🎲 Point Buy Calculator
⚙️ Click here to open the 5e Point Buy Calculator without leaving this page

  1. For your sheet, you have 3 options:

    • D&D Beyond: Which is the easiest if you're a beginner. If you choose this, please go to your folder in the Google Drive and put a link to your sheet in the red part in your tracking sheet. P.S. there's a thread for some tips on how to use it in 💬 getting-started channel
    • Dicecloud: Same as Beyond, please go to your folder in the google drive and put a link to your sheet in the red part in your tracking sheet.
    • G-sheet: In your Google Drive folder, there is a blank Gsheet that you can copy and rename it to your character's name. (you don't need to use this if you're using Beyond or Dicecloud)

  2. Post your character in the 💬 creation-log channel, using the pinned post for a template. Use this exact template 💬 Creation Log Template

    • A creation log cheat sheet is available in your folder to help you. For instructions on locating your folder, see the section titled 📁 “How to Find Your Folder”

    • And if you need help, feel free to open a ticket with the counselors to help you with the log 💬 create-a-ticket

    P.S. For races with multiple versions from different sourcebooks, you must list the source you are choosing.

  3. Once your character is ✅ Staff Approved, you receive the Player role, you are ready to play!

    P.S. Players can take either max gold from what their starting class gives them or starting equipment.

docs.title: How to Find Your Folder
docs.text:
If you still can't find your folder, make sure to check that:

  • you completed step one in the character-creation-steps .
  • you're logged in with the same Google account you used in the form during step one.

docs.title: Character Slots
docs.text: Players are allowed to have as many characters as they want, The only limitation is your creativity :D If you’re gonna be abusing it, remember, the gods of the Starry Shore are always watching!

docs.title: Live Sessions
docs.text:
1. DMs post their upcoming sessions in # looking-to-host . If you don't see a live session there that fits your schedule, you can ask if DMs are interested in hosting in the #looking-for-game channel. When you post in LFG, you can say something about your character(s), what kind of game you’re looking for and what times you can play.

  2. Follow the directions in the LTH post carefully. Each DM may require different information to join. Send the DM a private message to ask questions or with the information requested in their post.

  3. Enjoy the session!

  4. After the session, the DM will post a #session-log. You will need to update your character’s tracking sheet with your hours, items, and gold gained or lost in the session. If you have a disagreement with a DM, we encourage reaching out to them outside of the game to work things out. If there are still difficulties, or if this is not possible, please contact a staff member to help resolve the issue.

docs.title: Text Roleplay
docs.text:
Characters begin in the #main street. You can enter the main street in any fashion that fits your character. You can enter any 'scene' currently in progress and interact with other player characters. From there, they may enter a DM’s world in live sessions or remain in the main street. The Starry Shore is now that character’s home and a character that has the spell ‘Banishment’ cast on it will return to the main street. Each character may temporarily be in as many trp DM worlds as they want at once.

Every character in the Starry Shore has a mailbox in the #mail-boxes channel. Characters may put excess belongings into their cubby. Characters cannot peer into or mess with any other character’s cubby. However, a character may leave an item for another character in that character’s cubby. Any items shared between characters via their cubbies must be logged in #character-trade-log after the item has been left. If leaving an item in another character’s cubby, ping that Character.

@Starling (New Player) are restricted from joining both live TRP sessions and TRP worlds until they have lost the Starling role (reaching level 5).

After that, characters can enter any other world. Check out the #trp-world-directory to see a brief intro to each world written by the DM! Read pinned messages in the world's announcements channel for important information, including which room to enter the world through.

docs.title: TRP Rules
docs.text: Live TRP sessions grant rewards (hours and gold) at the same rate as standard live sessions.

docs.title: TRP/PBP DM Rules (in worlds)
docs.text:
5 players per TRP DM, 3 hrs per week x 1.5 DM bonus = 90 hrs/month max = equivalent of hosting a 4hr live session every other day (15 sessions)

DM Reward Guidelines - Each TRP/PBP DM can reward up to 5 players (one character each) in their world up to 3h per week, logging it in the DM rewards section to receive the DMing 1.5x bonus. (must participate for the rough equivalent of 3 hours, DM discretion, example below) - TRP sessions must always be logged as solo sessions, running the APL command with 1 entry will halve the gold; for DMs they need to check the solo box in their tracking sheet, and the logs need to be posted in #⁠trp-session-log channel using the template pinned there :D - 90h/month max for PBP DMing. This is equivalent to hosting a 4-hour live session every other day (15 sessions/month) - The content amount required is still the same. - More players or characters may still join if you allow, but they don't receive rewards.

for example: 💬 starting point to 💬 end is approximately 12 back and forth, approximately 2h total, which if we consider each reply from both parties is 5 min that's an hour worth of trp for each. DM discretion on how they evaluate the rewards, this is just an example and if you need help with that, you can open a ticket.

The 3-hour weekly reward is a maximum limit, not an automatic grant. DMs should award hours based on the actual amount of roleplay a player contributes during that week. If a player roleplays for more than 3 hours, they still only receive the maximum of 3 hours.

docs.title: TRP Player Rules
docs.text: 4 TRP worlds per player, 3h/week from each = 48 hrs/month max = equivalent of playing twelve 4hr live sessions per month - Each player is allowed to participate in up to 4 different TRP worlds. - They can get up to 3 hours per week from each world - A player can earn a maximum of 48 hours per month from TRP. This is equivalent to participating in twelve 4-hour live sessions per month - The TRP rewards logged should only be logged in your sheet after it gets approved with a ✅ by staff

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Players and DMs are welcome to provide anonymous feedback using the Member Feedback Form. This feedback may be complimentary, constructive criticism or complaints. Please note we take complaints seriously. Members may request their feedback by asking a staff member.

docs.title: Homebrew in the Starry Shore
docs.text:
Homebrew content is not allowed for official Starry Shore use. DMs may grant their players homebrew within their worlds. DM discretion applies, as always, to allowing homebrew from other DMs’ worlds into their sessions. To be used in a world other than that of the DM that granted it, the item must be posted in the homebrew-item-log by the DM granting the item. Other DMs have the freedom to allow or disallow homebrew at their own discretion, on a case-by-case basis. This decision is always made at the discretion of DMs, and pressuring DMs in either direction may constitute harassment.

DMs are restricted from giving homebrew to Starlings, to make it an easy and less confusing experience for new players!

docs.title: Character Leveling
docs.text:
Character levels are gained by playing in live or trp sessions. To advance a level, a character must be played in a number of hours equal to 2.5 times the current level. Hours needed to level are automatically calculated in the character tracking sheet supplied in the player folder. For example, a level 3 character needs to be played for 7.5 hours before advancing to level 4. A level 4 character needs to be played for 10 hours before advancing to level 5, etc.

Update your character tracking sheet following every live session you play. In addition, a current copy of the character sheet must always be kept in the player folder. Log any levels gained in #character-leveling-log using the pinned template.

There is no level cap on this server. Characters continue to level past level 20 using the hours-played formula above. Options for these characters are as follows: * Multiclassing: a character may continue to take levels in additional classes following multiclassing rules * Level 20 Retirement (see Character Retirement) * Prestige

docs.title: Subclass Change
docs.text:
You have two options to retrain and switch subclasses.

  1. Option 1 - DTP: A player may use 100 DTP and spend 500 gp per character level to switch to a different subclass. As per Tasha's, if a player switches back to a previous subclass they may forgo the gold costs and the DTP cost is halved.
  2. Option 2 - Session: A player may ask a DM to host a session for training to the new subclass. 500 gp per character level must be paid for this change and the session can give no loot rewards. Hours are given as usual and must level the character to a level in which they receive an ASI or Feat. Because they are training within a session no DTP will be required.

Each option must be documented using the template in #character-leveling-log, noting the subclass change made and which DM and Session provided the change.

docs.title: Character Respec
docs.text:
Players can make changes to the class, subclass, ability scores, background, race, feats, etc. up to 2 times per 6-month period (the first from January 1st to June 30th, the second from July 1st to December 31st) on the server. A character’s personal history and personality are not regulated by the mechanics of D&D and therefore do not require an official respec to develop and evolve overtime.

Submit the log into the #character-respec-log channel for approval. A reminder, you can play the respecced version of a character before it gets approved by staff.

You can change any of the following things using the respec option: * Character name * Character race and sub-race * Character class and subclass, including multiclass options * Feats * Ability Scores * Spells * Starting equipment packages * Background (personality, ideals, bonds, and flaws in addition to features, skill proficiencies, tool proficiencies, background equipment, and background gold) * Chosen Proficiencies (skills, tools, and languages) * Prestige purchases * Artifact properties

The following items cannot be changed through a character respec: * Level/hours * Amount of gold (except for background gold) * Equipment (except for starting equipment packages) * Magic Items and Consumables that have been received in sessions * Boons * Downtime points

Piety to a Deity is not automatically transferred if you change the character name and has to be logged in #piety-log with a link to the respec-log

docs.title: Character Prestige Options
docs.text:
A character of level 20+ can prestige their character, giving up levels and hours in exchange for Prestige Points to be used at the Prestige Shop.

For more info, check out 💎 2014 Prestige Rules

docs.title: Character Death (and other persistent effects)
docs.text:
If your character dies in a permadeath session, the DM will log it in the #death--log. They may specify that the character death is world-specific, but unless otherwise stated, your character is universally dead. In worlds where your character is dead, you may not play that character.

Aside from death, there are other persistent effects that may happen to your character. Limb loss, item loss, curses, ruidium corruption, and divine favor are some (but not all) of the things that might happen to a character and may be logged by a DM in #persistent-effects-log.

docs.title: What is Proxying?
docs.text: Proxying has 2 mechanics: 1. Hour Allocation: You can allocate session hours to a different character by indicating the desired character's name and level at the session's end. 2. Level Adjustment: Temporarily adjust your character's level for a session. It's recommended to use a duplicate character sheet labeled with the proxy level for clarity.

docs.title: Methods of Proxying
docs.text:
• The Fast Method: Directly level up your character and update your sheet with Avrae. This method carries the risk of forgetting to revert changes post-session.
  • The Safe Method: Create a new character sheet with the proxy level and import it to Avrae, minimizing the risk of accidental non-reversion.

docs.title: Magic Items and Proxying
docs.text: Acquiring magic items while proxying depends on the Dungeon Master (DM). Always confirm with your DM about any specific rules for proxying. Remember to remove any proxy-specific items after the session, as they do not carry over.

docs.title: Party Gold and Proxy Levels
docs.text: Party Gold earnings are based on the actual level of the character receiving the session hours, not the proxy level.

docs.title: Proxying Down
docs.text: With DM approval, you can proxy down to participate in lower-level sessions. Ensure you remove any high-tier items that become ineligible.

docs.title: Gold & Mundane Items: Purchasing and Selling
docs.text:
Characters can buy basic, mundane items (such as armor, weapons, and adventuring gear) that are listed in the Player’s Handbook (PHB) for the price listed in the PHB. This only needs to be logged in the character tracking sheet. Characters can also sell these items for half of the price listed in the PHB.

Characters can also buy and sell mundane items in a DM’s world, through trp and live sessions. Any gold found within a world can only be spent in that world, unless it is given as player loot for a session. Gold and mundane items gained within a world (not recorded as official session loot) is exclusive to that world and is considered homebrew elsewhere.

Mundane items and gold may also be granted as rewards for live sessions. Items and gold gained in this way can be used anywhere and must be logged on the character tracking sheet and by the DM in the trade log.

docs.title: Magic Items
docs.text:
Magic items may be received in live sessions as rewards up to the gold value of the session loot and chosen from The Starry Shore Shopping List. Magic items received as live session loot may be used server-wide, but some DMs have restrictions in their worlds. Magic items may only be received and used by characters of the same or higher tier.

Server-wide allowed magic items can be found in the 🛒 2014 Shopping Guide . Any item not on the shopping list is not allowed in The Starry Shore and is therefore considered homebrew within the server.

P.S. Any item that has a recharge time longer than 30 Days is no longer rechargeable but is considered a consumable instead.

docs.title: Notes about items
docs.text:
• Some powerful items have had their properties altered. These altered properties can be found in their listing in The Starry Shore Shopping List.
  • Characters may only use the manuals that boost ability scores once.

  • Some of these items require a session to obtain, due to their lore and power (“session required” in the shop). However, a character must still pay the gold cost to obtain the item.

    • A maximum of one session-required item can be obtained per session.
    • Only one player may receive a session-required item per session.
    • This applies whether the item is bought or crafted, and it cannot be traded.
    • Session-required items cannot be traded.
    • Example: if 2 characters need the same item, they still need 2 sessions to do so.

    These items are unique and important and it should be personalized and significant to the character gaining it, so to keep it like that, the session needs to be tailored about the character gaining it with exploration, combat, or solving puzzles, which can be more rewarding and immersive for the player getting it.

  • The player may request the beneficial properties of artifacts, and ultimately the DM of the session will determine the item’s beneficial and detrimental properties. The same properties may not be granted twice on a given item.

  • DMs may choose to rename the item, but both names must be logged.
  • Artifacts are limited to one per character except if prestige points have been used to purchase a second artifact slot.
    • To change artifacts, a character must first destroy their current artifact in a session, then acquire a new one in another session.
    • You can rent a 3rd artifact slot, check out 🕒 2014 DTP Guide for more info.
    • All of these items must be logged in #artifact-and-boon-purchase-log.

docs.title: Shopping: Purchasing Magic Items via Live Sessions or TRP
docs.text:
DMs may permit players to discover shops within their worlds, either during live sessions or through text-based roleplay (TRP), and purchase items from these lists found in other tabs. In these shops, players can purchase magical and mundane items.

Shops are permitted to charge more than the cost in the shopping list but cannot charge less. DMs retain full discretion over the availability of items, including what items are available and in what quantities. If the items are not listed in the shopping list, they will be considered homebrew within The Starry Shore.

For players seeking to purchase items, there are two methods:

  1. During alive session, if the DM allows it, players can submit a list of items they wish to purchase. To find the price of these items, check here: 🛒 2014 Shopping Guide

  2. Through TRP shops in the market district category or any other shops within TRP worlds, as well as VIP buildings. Players engage in TRP interactions to procure items and then send the list to the DM.

P.S. #the-starry-store-2nd-best-shop is ideal for quick item pickups, no TRP necessary. Slow mode is activated within the shop, so if your list isn’t logged yet, just update it instead of posting multiple entries.

DMs must post #magic-item-log entries for characters who purchase magic items in their sessions.

docs.title: Selling Magic Items via live session or TRP
docs.text:
Selling an item at 50% of its base gold value is free and does not require a check. It must be logged by a DM in the #magic-item-log .

Selling an item at 100% of its base gold value requires a check and costs DTP. The check is a Charisma (Persuasion) check with a DC equal to the item’s tier x 5. The DTP cost is also equal to the item’s tier x 5.

Buffs on the selling roll in live sessions are the same as crafting ones. See #downtime-rolls.

docs.title: Character Trading
docs.text: Characters can buy and sell to other characters as they wish. Characters can also gift items to other characters. It must be roleplayed in some fashion and logged in the #character-trade-log.

docs.title: Sending Stone System
docs.text:
Every character is gifted a sending stone upon their arrival to The Starry Shore. Sending stones can be linked to the sending stone of any other The Starry Shore resident that you have met.

Sending Stones use a "Contacts" system in place of needing to carry a half dozen or more stones. This way, a character in The Starry Shore only needs to physically carry a single sending stone. Make sure to gain the consent of the player whose character contact you wish to store.

docs.title: Boons
docs.text:
Characters may purchase from a limited selection of Epic Boons as detailed in the Boons spreadsheet for the gold listed. Characters must meet the listed level requirements. To purchase a boon, post in #artifact-and-boon-purchase-log using the provided template. A staff member must approve this purchase.

A character may only have a maximum of three boons, except if you buy a prestige boon slot. Boons belong to the character, not the player, and cannot be transferred to another character.

docs.title: Pets
docs.text:
Pets will require a bonus action to command to take their turns (except movement) as a default rule in the server, unless the DM said otherwise If you have a companion via class feature like drakewarden or steel defender, your bonus action command can apply to both your pet and your companion

  • Pets can be a maximum size of Medium and maximum Challenge Rating of ¼ all the way down to 0 CR.
  • Pets may be of Beast, Fey, Fiend, Construct or Dragon type.
  • Pets must have an intelligence of 3 or lower.
  • A character is limited to one maximum CR ¼ creature or two maximum CR ⅛ creatures.

P.S. Only the first pet (for each character) gains the upgrades from boosting or subscribing, the 2nd pet will always be CR 1/8 without any upgrades.

What happens when a pet dies? are they gone forever?

Nah, they spawn back in the Shore to be picked up for the next session. But they are out for the current mission unless they're revived.

docs.title: Server Booster Pet Perks
docs.text:
• CR can be up to 1/2
  • Size can be Large or smaller
  • Your pet can now be a Plant, Aberration, Ooze, Elemental, Monstrosity, beast, fey, fiend, construct or dragon.

making the options up to 215 pets to choose from!! The size increase allows some pets to serve as mounts!

docs.title: Server Supporter Pet Perks
docs.text:
• CR can be up to 3 for this pet
  • Intelligence can be up to 5 or lower
  • Size can be Large or smaller
  • Your pet can now be any type except giants

making the options up to 384 pets to choose from!!

docs.title: Downtime
docs.text:
When the starry shorians are just chillin in The Starry Shore, they can spend their free time in a variety of activities such as:

  • Copying spells
  • Learning new tools or languages
  • Working for gold
  • Religious service to awaken/exalt an item
  • Changing spells choices
  • Crafting
  • Learning dunamancy or contaminations spells
  • Worshiping a god for their blessings
  • Change your subclass
  • Renting a 3rd artifact

For more details check out the 🕒 2014 DTP Guide

docs.title: How to gain karma points
docs.text:
For Players

  • When someone you invite to join the server reaches level 4 ==> 16 pts
  • Sharing a DND Beyond campaign with all the source books (not all the adventures lol) required to make a character ==> 12 pts (you can get another 12 points when the first one is full, so let's all agree that sharing is caring)

For DMs:

  • Becoming a full DM (one time thing) ==> 6 pts
  • Having a new player @Starling (New Player) (anyone who hasn't reached level 5 on any characters yet) in your session ==> 2 pts for each player

docs.title: Clarification about The Shore nature & VIP building
docs.text:
The Starry Shore main bubble is created by the gods, and outside influence can't affect or harm shorians inside the bubble. If anyone (NPCs) not accepted by the gods enters, they immediately get disintegrated, unless they're lucky enough to be accepted to be a shorian (is converted into a PC).

Some of The Starry City (VIP) buildings can be outside the bubble but still close enough to receive limited protection... but yes, having it outside the shore would expose it to risks (since some DMs use it for their own sessions.)

docs.title: Rules for Simulacrum, Demiplane and Glyph of Warding
docs.text:
Due to their high propensity for abuse in a Westmarch-style setting such as ours, we have server-wide rules for the spells Simulacrum and Demiplane:

  1. Respec/Prestige also changes any active Simulacrum's statistics to reflect your new ones.

  2. To bring a Simulacrum or use a Demiplane in a session, the character must be able to cast the spell on their own.

  3. Simulacrums of other PCs can only be created with consent. These Simulacrums can only be brought in the session if the PC is also present and consents to it.

  4. Simulacrums are unable to cast the Simulacrum spell.

  5. Item Attunement Requirement: If the spell is cast through a magic item, the caster must be attuned to that item in the session.

  6. Spell Gem Restriction: To imbue the Spell Gem, the character is required to know the spell. Other creatures cannot imbue a Spell Gem on your behalf and any ongoing effects of it are lost once the attunement is broken with it.

  7. Ruby Weave Gem: The spell learned through the Ruby Weave Gem and any ongoing effects of it are lost once the attunement is broken with it.

Casting and interacting with these spells and their effects can take a considerable amount of time. As always, remember to spend and track DTP usage if you are using these spells outside of sessions.

P.S. Extradimensional Spaces created by items can not be used to store Glyph of Warding (e.g Bag of Holding, Portable Hole, etc)

docs.title: How to become a Dungeon Master (DM)
docs.text:
To become a DM, contact a staff member after you have reached level 4 on a player character, and you will receive the apprentice DM role. As an apprentice DM, you will need to host 5 open vc sessions, then you may receive the DM role.

We recommend posting about yourself in #dm-directory while you are an active DM. At any time, if you wish to take a break from DMing, you may request the staff team to remove the DM role.

Apprentice DMs are not able to run live trp sessions, create a trp world, give out homebrew, or running perma-death on sessions till they get their full dm tag (which requires running live vc sessions)

docs.title: DM Rewards
docs.text:
DMs earn rewards to be applied to their own characters when they run live sessions. For a given session, a DM chooses a single character to give these rewards to. Log the session in the second tab of your Character Tracking Sheet, labeled DM Rewards. The session rewards will be automatically added to the character’s hour, gold, and DTP totals.

DMs earn hours for running live sessions at a rate of: Session Length (in hours rounded to the nearest 30 minutes) x 1.5

DMs earn DTP rewards for running live sessions at a rate of: Session Length (in hours rounded to the nearest 30 minutes) x 4

DMs earn gold rewards as specified in the DM Rewards tab of your tracking sheet when you log the session.

  • This value is determined by the current level of the character that the DM is applying the session to and the length of the session.
  • Gold rewards are halved for sessions running less than two hours.
  • Gold rewards are multiplied by 1.5 for sessions that run for four or more hours.
  • Party members may choose to split loot amongst party members however DM and members see fit.

docs.title: Do:
docs.text:
1. Uphold the rules of the server.
  2. Give equal and generous treatment to all players.
  3. Make sure characters are approved and their character sheets are up to date before they play in your sessions.
  4. Maintain your logs in the following channels: LTH, session log, magic items log, boons log, death log

docs.title: Do Not:
docs.text:
1. Abuse player characters or kill them arbitrarily.
  2. Treat combat as You vs. Player.
  3. Delete the messages of other players in public channels outside of your own world category.
  4. Take staff duties upon yourself, such as messaging white names, approving characters, or deleting logs.

docs.title: Running Live Sessions
docs.text:
To run a live session, a DM should post in # looking-to-host using the pinned template. Players may post in # looking-for-game with requests for a game to be run. We recommend including a Discord Timestamp on your LTH post to overcome time zone misunderstandings.

Please use the session difficulty labels outlined here 💬 #looking-to-host

DMs can run sessions however they see fit. The session focus may vary. All games are run in Session Lobbies and Session Lobby Text under the Live Sessions category. DMs may use any supplemental materials to run their sessions, such as streaming a tabletop simulator or inserting ambiance via music bots, provided those materials are available to all players.

Players in live sessions are expected to be in-character. You cannot proxy as your in-real-life self, nor host a session for such play. Please use the ooc Misc (Out of Character) voice channels for ooc hanging out, watching movies, or any ooc activity that does not impact PC development.

docs.title: Session Loot
docs.text: DMs can offer rewards for their session as they see fit, up to the allowable loot value shown in the DM Rewards tab of their tracking sheet when they log the session. * Homebrew items given as session rewards can only be used in that DM’s world, except at other DMs’ discretion. * DMs can give less than the allowable loot value. This is a maximum value. Note that DMs cannot give items that are above the character’s tier.

docs.title: Solo Sessions
docs.text:
DMs may run 1-on-1 sessions with the following restrictions (these are automatically calculated when you check the “solo” box in the DM tracking sheet): * Player gold-equivalent loot maximum reduced to ½ of normal maximum allowance. * DM gold-reward reduced to ½ and be calculated as a player (no "DM multiplier" on gold reward).

This conversion is completed automatically in the DM Rewards.

docs.title: Session Hours & Tracking
docs.text:
The number of hours played is calculated by rounding to the nearest half hour and the average party level (APL) is rounded to the nearest whole number.

A DM may choose to charge DTP for activities a character participates in during one of their sessions.

Following every session, a DM must post in #session-log using the provided template. It is important to do this ASAP following a session.

Please note: in order to be counted in a session and gain loot and hours, you must play for at least one full hour.

docs.title: Astral Oasis Sessions
docs.text: Sessions taking place within The Starry Shore are referred to as “social sessions.” Normally role-play-centric, they may be set within the fight club, main street, Astral Oasis, VIP buildings, or other parts of The Starry Shore. These kinds of sessions don't reward players with any gold, and DMs have to log it in their sheets with the box in the middle that says solo/lounge.

docs.title: Buying Mundane items
docs.text:
Characters can buy basic, mundane items (such as armor, weapons, and adventuring gear) that are listed in the Player’s Handbook (PHB) for the price listed in the PHB.

This only needs to be logged in the character tracking sheet. Characters can also sell these items for half of the price listed in the PHB.

Some mundane items have prices listed in the Mundane Items tab.

docs.title: Buying Magic items
docs.text:
DMs may permit players to discover shops within their worlds, either during live sessions or through text-based roleplay (TRP), and purchase items from these lists found in other tabs. In these shops, players can purchase magical and mundane items.

Shops are permitted to charge more than the cost in the Cart but cannot charge less. DMs retain full discretion over the availability of items, including what items are available and in what quantities. If the items are not listed in the cart, they will be considered homebrew within The Starry Shore.

Characters are only permitted to buy items that are their Tier or lower.

For players seeking to purchase items, there are two methods:

  1. During a live session, if the DM allows it, players can submit a list of items they wish to purchase.
  2. Through shops in the market district category or any other shops within TRP worlds, as well as VIP buildings. Players engage in TRP interactions to procure items and then send the list to the DM.

P.S. #the-starry-store-2nd-best-shop is ideal for quick item pickups, no trp necessary. slow mode is activated within the shop, so if your list isn’t logged yet, just update it instead of posting multiple entries.

You can use our cart to make the list 🛒 2014 Item Shop

The list should look like this as an example: Example: Nyx buys: （1x） Cuddly Strixhaven Mascot 1,500 – 1,500 GP （1x） Talking Doll 100 – 100 GP Total: 1,600 GP Nyx, played by @promptferret

docs.title: How can i craft items?
docs.text: Please check out the ⚒️ Crafting page for more info

docs.title: Selling Magic Items via live session or TRP
docs.text:
Selling an item at 50% of its base gold value is free and does not require a check. It must be logged by a DM in the #magic-item-log .

Selling an item at 100% of its base gold value requires a check and costs DTP. The check is a Charisma (Persuasion) check with a DC equal to the item’s tier x 5. The DTP cost is also equal to the item’s tier x 5.

Buffs on the selling roll in live sessions are the same as crafting ones.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: • Any item that has a recharge time longer than 30 Days is no longer rechargeable but is considered a consumable instead.

docs.title: Crafting DCs
docs.text:
The difficulty class (DC) of a crafting check depends on the tier of the item being crafted. The higher the tier, the harder it is to craft. The DCs for each tier are:

Tier DC Tier 0 and Tier 1 11 Tier 2 15 Tier 3 19 Tier 4 23 Tier 5 27

docs.title: Crafting Costs
docs.text: The cost of crafting an item consists of two components: gold and downtime points (DTP). Gold is the amount of money required to buy the materials and tools needed for crafting. Downtime points represent the amount of time required to complete the crafting process.

docs.title: DTP Costs
docs.text: Tier Consumable Permanent T0 1 DTP 2 DTP T1 3 DTP 10 DTP T2 10 DTP 15 DTP T3 50 DTP 80 DTP T4 100 DTP 150 DTP T5 200 DTP 250 DTP

docs.title: Gold Costs
docs.text: • Half of the gold cost of the original item.

docs.title: Crafting Restrictions
docs.text:
There are some restrictions on what items can be crafted and how they can be crafted. These are:

  1. Artifacts cannot be crafted.
  2. Session-required items can only be crafted in a live session.
  3. Any buffs from items do not apply to crafting rolls.
  4. Outside of live sessions, only passive buffs from race/class/background features are allowed.

  5. In live sessions, only the following buffs are allowed (where applicable):

    • Help action from another player (they must also have an applicable tool proficiency)
    • Bardic Inspiration
    • Dark One's Own Luck
    • Bend Luck
    • Bolstering Magic
    • Emboldening Bond
    • Cosmic Omen
    • Psi-Bolstered Knack
    • Otherworldly Glamour
    • Any applicable Blood Hunter Mutagen buffs

docs.title: Tool Proficiencies Needed
docs.text:
To craft an item, a character must have proficiency with the appropriate tool for the item type. The tool proficiency determines what kind of check is made to craft the item. P.S. In sessions, DMs have freedom to decide what stat is used

Item Type Tool Proficiencies Applicable Ability Scores Armor Cobbler's, Leatherworker's, Smith's, Tinker's, Weaver's STR / DEX Adventure Gear Carpenter's, Leatherworker's, Smith's, Tinker's INT / WIS Ammunition Smith's, Tinker's, Woodcarver's DEX / WIS Potion / Poison Alchemist's, Brewer's, Herbalist's, Poisoner's CON / WIS Ring Glassblower's, Jeweler's, Tinker's DEX / CHA Scroll Calligrapher's, Forgery, Arcana Check DEX / INT Shield Carpenter's, Smith's, Woodcarver's STR / CON Wand / Rod Tinker's, Woodcarver's, Arcana Check INT / WIS / CHA Weapon Smith's, Tinker’s, Woodcarver's STR / DEX / CON Wondrous Item Any applicable tool, Arcana Check INT / CHA

docs.title: Crafting Outcomes
docs.text:
On a successful check, the item is crafted and the character spends the gold and DTP required for the item.

On a failed check, the GP and DTP costs are spent and the item is not crafted, however the character can attempt another check for an additional 1/4th the original GP and DTP cost.

docs.title: How to use tools
docs.text:
To learn a tool proficiency, use the command: !tool prof <tool_name>.

For expertise, use exp instead of prof.

Example: !tool prof alchemist

To make a check with the tool, use the command: !tool <tool_name> <stat>

Example: !tool alchemist wis

docs.title: The Starry Shore DownTime Points Guide (DTP)
docs.text:
When the starry shorians are just chillin in The Starry Shore, they can spend their free time in a variety of activities such as:

  • Change your name
  • Copying spells
  • Learning new tools or languages
  • Working for gold
  • Religious service to awaken/exalt an item
  • Changing spells choices
  • Crafting
  • Learning dunamancy or contamination spells
  • Worshiping a god for their blessings
  • Change your subclass
  • Renting a 3rd artifact

docs.title: How to gain DTP?
docs.text:
DTP is gained by 3 ways currently:

  • 2 DTP are added automatically every real-life day to your sheet once you log your first session
  • Hosting a session grants you DTP equal to 4 times the session's length in hours
  • Exchanging Karma pts to DTP

P.S. 1 DTP is equivalent to 8 hours of in-game time.

docs.title: Changing your Name
docs.text: You can use 1 DTP to legally change the name of your character across the multiverse.

docs.title: Copying spells for Wizards
docs.text:
Copying a Spell into the Book: When you find a wizard spell of 1st level or higher, you can add it to your spellbook if it is of a spell level you can prepare and if you can spare the time to decipher and copy it. For each level of the spell, the process takes 2 hours and costs 50 gp. (the gold and time you must spend to copy spells for some subclasses is halved.)

Copying from a Spell Scroll: A wizard spell on a spell scroll can be copied just as spells in spellbooks can be copied. When you copy a spell from a spell scroll, you must succeed on an Intelligence (Arcana) check with a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. If the check succeeds, the spell is successfully copied. Whether the check succeeds or fails, the spell scroll is destroyed.

Copying from another Spellbook: same as Copying from a Spell Scroll but it doesn't require a roll.

Example:

Character Name: random wizard name Downtime Activity: Copying Spells from someone else Cost: 350gp+2dtp Result: Copied 1st and 2nd level Wizard spells(detect magic, identify, comprehend languages, catapult, augury, detect thoughts, mind spike, locate object, see invisibility)

docs.title: Learning a new Language or a Tool Proficiency
docs.text:
Receiving training in a language or tool typically takes at least ten workweeks, but this time is reduced by a number of workweeks equal to the character's Intelligence modifier (an Intelligence penalty doesn't increase the time needed). Training costs 25 gp per workweek.

To see how much it would cost for your character to learn run the following command: !learning

docs.title: Working
docs.text:
When all else fails, an adventurer can turn to a Starry Shore worker to earn a living. This activity represents a character's attempt to find temporary work, the quality and wages of which are difficult to predict. Gaining Gold by using DTP depending on your character level and a roll of 3d10:

  • T1 - 3d10 x 20
  • T2 - 3d10 x 50
  • T3 - 3d10 x 100
  • T4 - 3d10 x 150
  • T5 - 3d10 x 200

!job <DTP amount you want to use> for example: toby have 30 dtp to spare: !job 30

docs.title: Religious Service
docs.text:
Character may perform religious service to gain favor with a god (DM discretion) or to awaken and exalt an item. The check (religion or persuasion) determines the benefits of service, as shown on the Religious Service table:

  • DC 1-10: 0 Favor
  • DC 11-20: 1 Favor
  • DC 21+: 2 Favor

P.S. this is not to worship the gods, that can be done in #⁠piety-log , this is for something like awaking and exalting items

!service <modifier> <# of Rolls(5 DTP per check)>

Modifier: religion or persuasion modifier (items are not applicable) Rolls: How many checks you wish to make in order to gain favor. This will determine the amount of DTP you use up. Each check costs 5 dtp. for example: toby wants to use 50 DTP to make 10 checks to gain favor and his religion mod is 3 !service 3 10

docs.title: Spell Change for Known casters
docs.text:
If your character is one of the classes that picks spells at level-up ( Bard, Eldritch Knight, Ranger, Arcane Trickster, Sorcerer, Warlock) and you regret your choices, you can spend that character's DTP and change your choices. The cost is based on the level of the spell you are learning, not the one you are losing.

  • Cantrips: 25 DTP
  • level 1 spells: 10 DTP
  • level 2 spells: 20 DTP
  • level 3 spells: 30 DTP
  • level 4 spells: 40 DTP
  • level 5 spells: 50 DTP
  • level 6 spells: 65 DTP
  • level 7 spells: 80 DTP
  • level 8 spells: 95 DTP
  • level 9 spells: 110 DTP

Post in ⁠#downtime-log with your character name, spell(s) lost, spell(s) learned and DTP cost, and be sure to track it on your tracking sheet. This is limited to once a month per character and up to three spells at a time.

docs.title: Dunamancy Spells
docs.text:
Who can access Dunamancy Spells? - Dunamancy spells are treated as wizard spells, but only Chronurgy and Graviturgy wizards can learn them through spellcasting/pact magic features without paying the DTP/GP cost. - Dunamancy learned through feats or class features other than spellcasting/pact magic do not have a DTP/GP cost. - Sorcerers, Bards, Warlocks, Rangers, Druids, Clerics, Artificers, Paladins, Arcane Trickster Rogues, Eldritch Knights, Profane Soul Blood hunters, and Heretic Jaeger can learn a Dunamancy spell instead or in place of another spell they would normally gain from their spellcasting/pact magic feature by following the rules below.

How to learn Dunamancy Spells? - Dunamancy spells can be learned by spending a number of weeks (1 week = 5 DTP) equal to the level of the spell (minimum of 1 week) and 50gp per week of research, and it must be logged in ⁠#downtime-log (unless you're Chronurgy or Graviturgy wizard)

  • The spell must be of a level that the character can prepare or learn in the class being used to learn the spell, and cannot be a cantrip.

  • To learn a Dunamancy spell, the character makes an Intelligence check; The DC of the check equals 10 + the spell’s level. The character can add a +1 bonus per additional 100 GP spent, to a maximum of +6.

How to add them: If the check succeeds the character learns the spell in a manner based on their class:

  • Wizards: Wizards add the spell directly to their spellbook
  • Known Casters: (sorcerers, warlocks, bards, rangers, arcane tricksters, eldritch knights, Profane Soul Blood hunters, and Heretic Jaeger) can change one of their known spells to the newly learned spell.
  • Prepared Casters: (Artificers, Druids, Clerics, Paladins) add the spell to the list of spells they can prepare.
  • Warlocks: Warlocks can replace a mystic arcanum for spells level 6, 7, 8 & 9, with the newly learned spell.

P.S. Anyone who has learned a Dunamancy spell can cast that spell from scrolls as normal

docs.title: Drakkenheim Spells
docs.text:
Spells from Drakkenheim are strictly guarded secrets, and not immediately available to just any caster. These spells cost 5 DTP and 250 GP per level of the spell to research, with some having prerequisites as well.

Who can access Drakkenheim Spells?

  • Drakkenheim spells are class-specific, and only their listed classes may research them.
  • Drakkenheim spells cannot be learned through feats or class features, and cannot be replicated by things like Wish or Mizzium Apparatus.
  • The spell must be of a level that the character can prepare or learn in the class being used to learn the spell.
  • Some Drakkenheim spells have additional prerequisites to learning them, listed below. These spells require a session to complete the research, and DMs should log these spells in #⁠persistent-effects-log when a player successfully learns them in-session. The player still logs the research in ⁠#downtime-log
  • Once research is complete, the character may prepare the spell, add it to their spellbook, or replace a spell they already know with the new spell, as appropriate for the spellcasting features of their class.
  • Due to their dependency on Delirium as a material component, scrolls and spellwrought tattoos cannot be made for Drakkenheim spells.

Drakkenheim spells by level:

  • 1st:
    • Delirium Orb [Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard]
  • 2nd:

docs.title: Gods of The Starry Shore!
docs.text:
The gods of Theros The Starry Shore are far more active than the deities of most D&D worlds and can reach all multiverses. But that doesn't mean they are ordinary creatures, they aren't mere mortals, nor are they monsters that can be fought.

The idea of the existence of gods, as it grew in popularity among the mortals of Theros, didn't bring the gods into being by itself. Mortal reverence and worship turned universal ideas into deities. It wasn't until mortals trusted the gods to act on their behalf, in response to sacrifices and prayers

Introducing:

  • Athreos, god of passage https://5e.tools/deities.html#athreos_theros_mot
  • Ephara, god of the polis https://5e.tools/deities.html#ephara_theros_mot

  • Tyr, God of Justice https://5e.tools/deities.html#tyr_faerûnian_scag

What do I gain from worshiping one?! The gods do reward the devotion of their champions, though. The strength of your devotion to your god is measured by your piety score. As you increase that score, you gain blessings from your god. Check the end of the god page or the threads in ⁠#gods-info to find out what each god grants their Devotee (3+ Piety), Votary (10+ Piety), Disciple (25+ Piety), Champion (50+ Piety), check the next part to learn how to unlock them.

I have enough piety! How do I unlock their blessings?! Gods grant their blessing to their worshipers based on how many followers there are in their temple! So, if you're looking to become a devotee, votary, disciple or champion to get their blessings, you need to have the same number of members of the same piety level to gain their blessings

For example: Matcha has 10 favors and wants to be a votary, she needs 9 more people who each have at least 10 favors to unlock the votary blessings for this temple. From that point on, all characters who have 10 favors will receive the devotee blessing once they gain 10 favors. No blessing is unlocked for you till a number of characters have enough piety to unlock that blessing.

To get the 3 piety feature, you would need 3 characters with at least 3 favor to unlock it!

How do I join their temple and start worshiping one of them?! and how do I gain piety/favor?! Well that's simple, check the pinned msgs in #⁠piety-log.

Oh that's cool! Is there a place where I can text role play to invite more characters to worship my god?! Of course, there will be a shrine for each god, and a thread for trp!

Just a shrine!! I want a whole temple for my god!! good news, For our amazing subscribers, your VIP building can become the main building for one of the gods! making it the main place for trp and the shrine will be moved to the temple meaning the thread will be closed!

Can I worship a different god after I worship another one? and do I keep my favors? Yes, you can, same as before just post a new entry in ⁠#piety-log, sadly the piety wouldn't carry over, favors gained for a certain god stays for that god, but you don't lose them in case you want to come back to worship that god!! but there might be consequences if you keep switching. GODS ARE NOT A JOKE!!

Diminishing your Deity's Influence The pantheon's power comes from peoples' collective belief in the values they represent. If you take actions in TRP or live sessions that diminish your diety's influence (as outlined for each deity), you may lose piety. Recommendations are -1 piety for minor infractions, -3 for major infractions, and -5 for severe infractions (DM discretion). Any piety losses should be logged in ⁠⁠#piety-log by the DM using the template pinned in that channel.

I respect these gods but none of them fits me! Can I worship a different god that's not from this list? And how do I get any blessing? Well, if you would like to worship Bahamut, God of Justice and Nobility for example, you need to get a temple and 25 characters to worship him and have 10 piety, and he will be added officially and the staff team will write up their blessing!

docs.title: Prestige Rules
docs.text:
Hey there! Did you know that once your player character (PC) reaches level 20 or higher, you have an alternative retirement option called Prestige. Using this system, you can trade in some of your hard-earned levels in exchange for prestige points (PP), which you can then use to purchase extra benefits for your PC. However, if your PC is below level 20, they won't be eligible for Prestige just yet.

If you do decide to Prestige your PC, you can return them to the start of any tier (which are levels 3, 5, 11, 17, and 23) and earn PP based on which tier you choose. This is a great way to get more benefits for your PC by trading in some of your hours. The PP you earn will be shown on your Tracking Sheet once you reach level 20. A character may prestige multiple times, each time returning to lower level and beginning their journey anew.

Just keep in mind that some items or abilities may be level-locked or tier-locked, meaning you can only benefit from them if your PC is at the appropriate level or tier.

So to explain what happens when you choose to Prestige your PC. It's a pretty big change, so it's important to understand what you get to keep. Here's the list of things you can hold on to:

  • Memories
  • Gold
  • DTP (this includes learned tools and languages)
  • Items (tier-locked)
  • Boons (tier-locked)
  • Artifacts (tier-locked)
  • The effects of manuals you previously used (tier-locked)
  • Any Prestige Points from previous Prestiges

docs.title: How to prestige:
docs.text:
You will need to post a log in the #character-retirement-and-prestige-log channel. Then a staff will review the prestige log.

Players can later use a character respec to revise their PP allocations if they so choose.

Players can also use karma points to get prestige points!!

docs.title: About the Server       The Starry Shore
D&D 5.5 Edition Westmarch Server (2024/5e)
docs.text:
Join The Starry Shore 2014/5e

Welcome to The Starry Shore Discover an endless number of worlds to explore at The Starry Shore! A place of respite adrift in the Astral Sea, the Starry Shore's magical barriers keep the typical dangers at bay, providing a sanctuary for any and all travelers who seek it. Adventure through new and exciting worlds via mysterious portals, or kick back with some friends and enjoy the Shore's amenities. We welcome travelers of all shapes and sizes and from all walks of life, so come let your imagination soar at The Starry Shore!

docs.title: How Things Work here?
docs.text:
Player Characters (PCs) exist in The Starry Shore, an interplanar hub with the main street leading to many portals. Dungeon Masters create those portals leading to whatever worlds they dream up. PCs can visit those worlds via live sessions and/or text role play (trp). PCs earn levels and gold via hours played in live sessions. Characters continue to level past level 20 using the hours-played formula. Though their level will not increase any further, they will gain additional rewards for each level:

  • 21, 22, 23: An Epic Boon each
  • 24: The ability to earn an artifact rarity item for your character
  • 25-30: A +2 increase to one ability score and its maximum.

and if you'd like to see how active the server is check out the 💬 session-log channel or the statistics in the 💬 announcements channel.

docs.title: What kind of D&D we play here?
docs.text:
Most of the games offered here are exciting one-shots, perfect for those who love spontaneous adventures. There are a few DMs that host campaigns, Typically, they like to play a few sessions with new players to see if there’s a good fit. If they like your gaming style, they might invite you to join a campaign. This server mainly focuses on these one-shot games, which make up the majority of our activities, allowing you to play on your own schedule.

We’re proud to say that our community only includes the coolest players. That said, we embrace diversity in play styles. Whether you’re someone who revels in rich storytelling and immersive roleplay, or a strategist who enjoys optimizing characters to their fullest potential, you’ll find a welcoming space here. Everyone is invited to bring their unique approach to the game.

docs.title: Modes of Play:
docs.text:
1. Live Voice Sessions: You gain "hours played", gold, and items as rewards from playing. (We use "hours played" in place of experience for leveling up.) This is the main method of play. And these kind of sessions can be anything, from lighthearted and funny to dark and serious.

  2. Text Roleplay: or TRP, there's 2 types of it:

  3. PBP/TRP in DMs worlds: This for casual trp, you can role play whenever you're free and the dm does the same.
  4. Trp for fun: This is the trp that happens inside the starry shore (Crossroad category, Starry City category)
Sounds great! How do I start? You must be 18 years of age or older to play on the server. Then follow the steps in 💬 #getting-started channel to make a character.

docs.title: Member Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Have common sense, and follow the Server Code of Conduct.
  • You must be 18 years of age or older to play on the server (This is both for social and legal reasons. Sorry, no exceptions.).
  • PVP requires consent from both parties including the DM. Consent needs to be communicated, not just implied.
  • Sexual themes are not allowed until consent from the whole party is given.
  • Adult themes and language may appear. Our DM worlds' range from lighthearted and funny to dark and serious.
  • You need an approved character in order to play (see 💬 getting-started channel).
  • Players must track their characters (level, gold, items, etc) and keep this information updated in the player folder provided, as well as the relevant log channels.
  • In a rules dispute between a DM and Player, the DM’s word goes until the session is over and the staff can mediate.

[!question] Unsure of something? Ask away! Our community is welcoming, knowledgeable, and happy to help.

docs.title: Open Door Policy
docs.text: The staff team’s goal is to promote a safe and fun environment for all server members. You are invited to contact any staff through voice or private messages with questions or concerns as you see fit. You can submit your thoughts any time through the 💬 create-a-ticket ⁠channel, where the staff team will have access to it for review and response.

docs.title: Crafting DCs and Costs
docs.text:
The difficulty class (DC) of a crafting check is determined by the item’s price, more powerful items are harder to craft. Crafting an item requires gold and downtime points (DTP), which represent material costs and time spent crafting.

  • Gold Cost: Half the gold cost of the original item
  • Downtime Point (DTP) Cost: Item cost ÷ 2 ÷ 25 (1 DTP = 25 gp)
  • Crafting DC: 10 + (item cost ÷ 450), rounded down

You can use the following tool to see all of the above once you put the item cost and click the "Calculate Crafting Costs" button

docs.title: Crafting Restrictions
docs.text:
There are some restrictions on what items can be crafted and how they can be crafted. These are:

  1. Artifacts cannot be crafted.
  2. Session-required items can only be crafted in a live session.
  3. Any buffs from items do not apply to crafting rolls.
  4. Outside of live sessions, only passive buffs from race/class/background features are allowed.

  5. In live sessions, only the following buffs are allowed (where applicable):

    • Help action from another player (they must also have an applicable tool proficiency)

docs.title: Tool Proficiencies Needed
docs.text:
To craft an item, a character must have proficiency with the appropriate tool for the item type. The tool proficiency determines what kind of check is made to craft the item. P.S. In sessions, DMs have freedom to decide what stat is used

docs.title: Crafting Outcomes
docs.text:
On a successful check, the item is crafted and the character spends the gold and DTP required for the item.

On a failed check, the GP and DTP costs are spent and the item is not crafted, however the character can attempt another check for an additional 1/4th the original GP and DTP cost.

docs.title: How to use tools
docs.text:
To learn a tool proficiency, use the command: !tool prof <tool_name>.

For expertise, use exp instead of prof.

Example: !tool prof alchemist

To make a check with the tool, use the command: !tool <tool_name> <stat>

Example: !tool alchemist wis
